doc.title: Stanley Kay interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001

title: Radio as a school for learning bands
summary: Kay describes listening to radio remotes from hotels and his lasting gratitude for music.

bands.name: Horace Heidt and his Musical Knights

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Radio had such a big role at that time, didn’t it?
With all those live broadcasts and all that.

Yeah well that’s where you learned. I mean I’d get in the bed, at one o’clock, I’d put my little radio on, of course they were doing remotes from all over the place. You know, “high on the top of the Astor roof we’re presenting Tommy Dorsey.” Or, “Horace Heidt and his Musical Knights.” Whatever they did. So, no, I loved it, and I love it today. I talk with the same enthusiasm as I did back then. Because music is, I’m very grateful for it. It has been very good for me, I’ve gotten to go all over the world because of music. I mean I know people that haven’t been over to Jersey yet and have been in New York. I’ve been all over the place. So I’m happy.
